import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL']:
 print(name, bool(importlib.util.find_spec(name)))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for name in ['manuscript.txt']+[f'page-{i:02d}.png' for i in range(1,13)]:
 (p/name).unlink()
p.rmdir()
try: p.parent.rmdir()
except OSError: pass
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important evaluation issue in brain-to-text decoding: repeated stimuli and overlapping temporal windows can inflate apparent generalization.
Holding out both subjects and stimuli is appropriate for evaluating decoding on unseen people and unseen language material. The graph illustrations communicate this evaluation goal effectively.

Examines both fMRI and EEG datasets, representative decoding models, and several splitting strategies. Four split seeds for overlap measurements and some implementation details provide useful starting points for replication.
weaknesses: The supplied algorithms do not enforce the central zero-leakage guarantee. Algorithm 1, line 15 checks whether a subject is held out but does not exclude held-out texts when restoring edges; Algorithm 2, line 33 has the corresponding omission for subjects. These rules can reintroduce overlap. The prose and pseudocode also disagree about graph construction. Corrected algorithms and explicit pairwise disjointness checks are necessary.

Reported evaluation results contain substantive inconsistencies. Table 4 gives EEG2Text ROUGE-1 recall/precision/F1 as 23.98/23.95/25.74; several Table 3 rows similarly report F1 exceeding both precision and recall, which is impossible under consistently aggregated standard F1. Additionally, Equation 8 measures exact signal intersection although the stated concern is shared subjects: disjoint EEG recordings can share subjects without intersecting as signals. The metric definitions, implementations, and tables require reconciliation.

The blanket characterization of existing protocols as suffering from leakage is overstated. Subject overlap can be appropriate when evaluating new stimuli for known individuals, and stimulus overlap can support evaluation of transfer across subjects for known material. The proposed joint holdout addresses a stricter generalization question; it does not establish that evaluations targeting these other settings are inherently invalid.

The experiments do not adequately isolate the claimed damage from leakage. Table 2 changes encoder initialization, learning rate, and training duration together. Improving evaluation scores or decreasing validation loss alone does not establish overfitting or encoder degradation. Matched training conditions and shuffled-signal or no-signal controls are needed to distinguish memorization, language-model contributions, and information obtained from brain activity. The inference protocol also needs to state explicitly whether generation uses reference prefixes.

The stated aims of maximizing data utilization and improving generalization are not demonstrated. The method discards observations, but retained sample counts, achieved partition sizes, and comparisons with simpler joint subject/stimulus partitions are absent. A maximal edge extension is not evidence of globally optimal retention, and changing the evaluation split does not itself demonstrate improved model generalization.

Reproducibility is insufficient for the proposed benchmark. The manuscript claims a release without providing a repository or split manifests, omits final subject/story/sample counts after filtering and partitioning, and reports no variability across training runs or held-out subjects for decoding results. Four seeds are reported only for overlap measurements. Together with the algorithm and metric inconsistencies, these gaps prevent a sound Findings recommendation; correcting the implementation and reporting and conducting controlled reruns appears feasible for the next cycle.
